Pumpkin Spice Sugar Cookies

By Michele Feuerborn on Oct 1, 2026 | Updated on Oct 1, 2026

When autumn arrives, nothing beats the cozy aroma of pumpkin spice filling the kitchen.

If you looking for a fun, fall sweet treat to bring to a school party, or a neighborhood potluck, these Pumpkin Sugar Cookies will be a massive hit with both kids and adults.

These frosted pumpkin cookies are beautiful pumpkin-shaped cut out cookies made with a homemade pumpkin spice mix, and topped with a maple glaze and cinnamon sugar.

While many pumpkin recipes turn out cakey, this recipe is specifically designed to give you a soft, tender cookie packed with real pumpkin flavor. They are the perfect festive fall treat for Halloween parties and your Thanksgiving dessert table.

Why You'll Love These Cut-Out Pumpkin Cookies

  • Festive Pumpkin Shapes: The dough holds its shape beautifully in the oven, so your holiday cookies look wonderful on the plate.
  • Irresistibly Soft Texture: A little bit of cornstarch mixed into the flour creates an incredibly soft, melt-in-your-mouth texture.
  • Rich Holiday Flavor: Making your own pumpkin spice mix gives these cookies a deep, comforting autumn flavor.

Ingredients For the Ultimate Pumpkin Cookies

For the Homemade Pumpkin Spice Mix

  • 1 tsp ground cinnamon
  • ½ tsp ground ginger
  • ¼ tsp ground allspice
  • ¼ tsp cloves
  • ⅛ tsp ground nutmeg

For The Pumpkin Sugar Cookies

  • ½ cup pumpkin puree (Make sure to use plain pumpkin puree, not pumpkin pie filling)
  • 1 cup unsalted butter, softened
  • 1 cup light brown sugar
  • 1 large egg
  • 2 tsp vanilla extract
  • 3 cups all-purpose flour (Measured using the spoon-and-level method)
  • 2 tbsp cornstarch
  • 1 tsp baking soda
  • ½ tsp salt

For the Silky Maple Cinnamon Glaze

  • 2 cups powdered sugar
  • 3 tbsp pure maple syrup (Avoid pancake syrup for the best flavor)
  • 2 tbsp milk
  • 1 tbsp butter, melted
  • 1 tsp vanilla extract
  • ½ tsp ground cinnamon
  • ⅛ tsp maple extract
  • Pinch of salt

Step By Step Instructions

1. Homemade Pumpkin Spice Mix

In a small bowl stir together all the ingredients for Pumpkin Spice Mix. Set aside.

2. Blot The Pumpkin

Scoop the 1/2 cup pumpkin puree onto a few layers of paper towels to let the extra moisture drain. Press down with fresh paper towels until the excess liquid is absorbed. Removing this moisture is key to keeping the cookies soft and tender instead of cakey.

3. Cream Butter and Sugar

In a large mixing bowl, beat the softened, unsalted butter and light brown sugar together with your electric mixer for 3 to 4 minutes until the mixture looks light and fluffy.

4. Mix The Wet Ingredients

Add the blotted pumpkin puree, the whole egg, and the vanilla extract to the butter mixture. Beat on medium speed until everything is smooth and combined.

5. Add the Dry Ingredients

In your medium bowl, whisk together the flour, cornstarch, baking soda, and your Homemade Pumpkin Spice Mix. Gradually mix these dry ingredients into your wet bowl just until a soft cookie dough forms.

6. Chill The Dough

Divide the dough into two equal halves. Shape each half into a flat disk, wrap them tightly in plastic wrap, and pop them in the fridge to chill for at least 45 minutes. Chilling the dough keeps it from sticking to your counter.

7. Roll and Cut Out Your Pumpkin-Shaped Cookies

Preheat your oven to 350°F and line your baking sheets with parchment paper. Lightly flour your counter. Roll the chilled dough out until it is about a ¼-inch thick. Cut out your shapes with your pumpkin cookie cutter and place them 2 inches apart on the baking sheets. If the dough starts to get too soft while you are working, just put it back in the fridge for 15 minutes to firm up.

8. The Quick Pre-Bake Chill

For the prettiest shapes, put the baking sheets with your cut-out cookies right back into the fridge for 10 to 15 minutes before they go into the oven. This extra chill keeps them from spreading out too much while baking.

9. Bake and Cool

Bake at 350°F for 10 to 12 minutes. They are ready when the centers look set and the bottoms are just slightly golden. Let them cool on the baking sheets for 5 minutes before moving them to a wire rack to cool completely.

10. Glaze The Cookies

In a small bowl, whisk the powdered sugar, melted butter, pure maple syrup, milk, vanilla extract, maple extract, cinnamon, and a pinch of salt together until smooth. Drizzle or spread the glaze over the cooled cookies. Let the glaze dry completely before serving or stacking them.

  • Fun Decorating Ideas: You can melt a few chocolate chips, put them in a small plastic baggie, snip off a tiny corner, and draw little vines at the top of each pumpkin stem. You can also mix ¼ cup of white sugar with 1 teaspoon of ground cinnamon and sprinkle it over the fresh wet glaze.

Tips for the Best Soft Iced Pumpkin Cookies

  • Try Browned Butter: For a rich, caramel-like flavor in your glaze, brown the 1 tablespoon of butter in a small pan before whisking it into your powdered sugar.
  • Don’t Skip the Chilling: Chilling the dough twice keeps the cookies easy to handle and helps them keep their distinct pumpkin shape in the oven.
  • Better the Next Day: These cookies taste amazing right away, but the warm spices and sweet maple glaze taste even better after the cookies sit in a container overnight.
  • Cozy Pairings: Serve these beautiful iced pumpkin cookies with a hot mug of apple cider, a warm cup of coffee, or a glass of cold milk.

Frequently Asked Questions About Pumpkin Sugar Cookies

Can I make this cut-out pumpkin cookie dough ahead of time?

Yes. You can prepare the cookie dough, wrap the disks tightly in plastic wrap, and store them in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. When you are ready to roll and cut out your pumpkin shapes, let the dough sit on the counter for a few minutes to soften slightly so it doesn’t crack.

Why do I only use 1/2 cup of pumpkin?

Real pumpkin contains a lot of water. Using a modest amount keeps the dough stable enough to roll and cut out into fun shapes while still providing plenty of authentic pumpkin flavor.

How do I know exactly when these iced pumpkin cookies are done baking?

Look for the centers to look dull and completely set rather than wet or shiny. The edges should look firm, and the bottoms will have just a hint of pale golden color. Avoid waiting for the tops to brown, or the cookies will lose their signature soft, melt-in-your-mouth bite.

Why do I need to blot the pumpkin puree for pumpkin sugar cookies?

Canned pumpkin is naturally full of moisture. In a cut-out recipe, excess water turns into steam during baking, which makes the cookies turn out cakey or rise into puffy blobs. Blotting the puree with a paper towel removes that liquid, allowing you to get real pumpkin flavor and a tender, soft texture without losing your clean cookie shapes.

Why is chilling the cookie dough before baking so important?

Chilling the cut-out cookies right on the baking sheets solidifies the butter. If the butter is cold when it hits the 350°F oven, the cookies will hold their festive pumpkin shapes perfectly. If the dough is warm, the fat melts too quickly, causing the cookies to spread out flat on the pan.

Storing and Freezing Pumpkin Spice Sugar Cookies

  • Room Temperature: Store in an airtight container for up to 5 days.
  • Refrigerator: Keep in the fridge for up to 1 week.
  • Freezer: You can freeze the plain, unglazed cookies for up to 3 months. Let them thaw out to room temperature before adding your fresh glaze.

Recipe

Pumpkin Sugar Cookies

By Michele Feuerborn
No ratings yet
These beautiful pumpkin-shaped cut out pumpkin cookies feature a warm, homemade pumpkin pie spice mix and a silky maple cinnamon glaze. They are the perfect fall festive treat for Halloween parties, school events, and Thanksgiving dessert tables!

Prep Time 35 minutes minutes
Cook Time 10 minutes minutes
Chill 45 minutes minutes
Total Time 1 hour hour 30 minutes minutes
Servings 24 cookies
Calories 219
Prevent your screen from going dark

Ingredients

For the Pumpkin Spice Mix

  • 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
  • 1/2 teaspoon ground ginger
  • 1/4 teaspoon ground allspice
  • ¼ teaspoon cloves
  • 1/8 teaspoon ground nutmeg

For the Pumpkin Sugar Cookies

  • 1/2 cup pumpkin puree
  • 1 cup unsalted butter, softened
  • 1 cup light brown sugar
  • 1 large egg
  • 2 teaspoons vanilla extract
  • 3 cups all-purpose flour
  • 2 tablespoons cornstarch
  • 1 teaspoon baking soda
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt

For the Maple Cinnamon Glaze

  • 2 cups powdered sugar
  • 3 tablespoons pure maple syrup
  • 2 tablespoons milk
  • 1 tablespoon butter, melted
  • 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
  • 1/2 teaspoon ground cinnamon
  • 1/8 teaspoon maple extract
  • Pinch salt

Instructions 

Make the Pumpkin Spice Mix

  • In a small bowl stir together all the pumpkin spice mix ingredients

Make the Pumpkin Sugar Cookie Dough

  • Place the pumpkin puree on a paper towel and let all the moisture drain. Repeat with dry paper towels until all the moisture is gone.
  • In a large mixing bowl, beat the softened butter, and brown sugar until light and fluffy, about 3 to 4 minutes.
  • Beat in the pumpkin puree, egg, and vanilla extract until smooth.
  • In a separate bowl, whisk together the flour, cornstarch, baking soda, salt, and pumpkin pie spice.
  • Gradually mix the dry ingredients into the wet ingredients just until a soft dough forms.
  • Chill the Cookie Dough: Divide the dough in half and shape each half into a disk. Wrap tightly and refrigerate for at least 45 minutes.
  • Preheat the oven to 350°F.
  • Line baking sheets with parchment paper.
  • Lightly flour your work surface and roll the dough to about 1/4-inch thickness.
  • Cut the dough with a pumpkin-shaped cookie cutter and place the cookies about 2 inches apart on the prepared baking sheets.
  • For the sharpest edges, refrigerate the cut cookies on the baking sheets for 10 to 15 minutes before baking.
  • Bake for 10 to 12 minutes, or until the cookies are set and the bottoms are just beginning to turn lightly golden.
  • Cool on the baking sheets for 5 minutes before transferring to a wire rack to cool completely.

Make the Maple Glaze

  • To make the glaze, whisk together the powdered sugar, butter, maple syrup, milk, vanilla extract, maple extract, cinnamon, and salt until smooth. If needed, add a little more milk for a thinner glaze or additional powdered sugar for a thicker glaze.
  • Drizzle the tops of the cooled cookies with the glaze.
  • Allow the glaze to set completely before serving.

  • Refrigerator: Keep in the fridge for up to 1 week.
  • Freezer: You can freeze the plain, unglazed cookies for up to 3 months. Let them thaw out to room temperature before adding your fresh glaze.
